issue.author: ht-admin
issue.body:
Round 1 of at least three on the paper-writing worker of the positions paper-repo and internal-review-repo of the research world rw_313df9cf84a4 (PaperWrite-Bench paper_29, given to you to read). The aim over the rounds is a curve: each round's kept worker writes better than the last. This world is one round: one diagnosis, at most two candidates, one comparison, one decision.

Where we start. The last world kept cand-a, now published and merged in a-green-hand-jack/HuTian-Workers as cand-a-writer@v1 (paper-repo) and cand-a-reviewer@v1 (internal-review-repo): incumbent@v3 (Claude Code, claude-sonnet-5-5, effort low) plus a CLAUDE.md of writing and review norms. On the held-out paper it raised the blind score from 26.4 to 30.8 of 32 and the verifier reward from 0.886 to 0.900, but it writes longer papers (11 pages in 2 of 5 runs against the 9-page target) and its section_score fell from 0.96 to 0.88. cand-a is the incumbent of this round; the original incumbent@v3 is the curve's origin.

The rubric first. The 32-point rubric can no longer decide: cand-a's mean 30.8 plus its spread 2.0 is above the maximum, so no candidate could ever pass. Before anyone looks at a manuscript made in this world, the task-setter writes rubric v2 with room above cand-a. Its items and the levels of each item come from what the task and the benchmark ask of a paper: the page limit and venue in each task's metadata and template, the required sections the task instruction lists (abstract, introduction, related work, method, experiments, limitations, conclusion), the template's format kept, every claim grounded in the supplied overview, the supplied figures and tables used and interpreted, citations from the given bibliography that fit their sentences; plus how well the paper argues and reads. Every level has an anchored description so two judges would give the same score. It must apply unchanged to any PaperWrite-Bench paper (numbers such as the page limit are read from each task), not only paper_29 or paper_39, and it must not be shaped around cand-a's weaknesses. Freeze it: put it in the task-setter's release with its sha256, and do not change it in this or any later round. Scores under the old rubric stay as they are, for the record.

Diagnosis. The sparring-partner runs the incumbent cand-a twice on the training paper, continuing rw_313df9cf84a4 from c0, for the diagnostician; the diagnostician diagnoses what cand-a still does badly in writing, from those runs, from the earlier paper_29 runs, and from the judge's summary of the last world's comparison (aggregate scores per worker and item, no held-out manuscripts). The tuner makes at most two candidates from the diagnosis, each starting from cand-a: only the worker's content and settings change (assets, instructions, effort and other settings of Claude Code); the agent and the model stay Claude Code and claude-sonnet-5-5; at least one candidate changes writing content through assets, and one that changes only a setting says so. Nothing in a candidate may be about a particular paper.

Comparison and decision. The judge runs, from c0 of rw_19be25bd2f7d (paper_39, ACL 2025) and all at the same time, five runs each of incumbent@v3, cand-a and every candidate: twenty worlds with two candidates. If the provider answers with overloads or the host refuses, start them in two batches with the same mix of workers and say so. Judge every manuscript with the frozen rubric v2, blind (random labels before reading, unblinded after all are scored), and with the verifier (reward and every component), as before. Keep a candidate only if its blind mean under v2 is above cand-a's mean by more than cand-a's spread (max minus min of its runs) and its verifier mean is not below cand-a's; if both pass, keep the better and say why; if none passes, cand-a stays and the record says on which measures the difference stayed within the spread. Record for every worker the v2 blind mean, min, max and spread, the mean of each item, and the verifier mean, min, max and every component, in a round summary in the judge's repository. After the decision is recorded, the diagnostician and the tuner may read that summary for the next round, but not the manuscripts.

Who reads what. rw_19be25bd2f7d, every world made from it, the heldout-material resource, the paper_39 verifier files in your inputs and the held-out manuscripts belong to the task-setter and the judge alone: the sparring-partner, the tuner and the diagnostician do not read any of them.

Put back. The sparring-partner puts the kept worker back by continuing rw_313df9cf84a4 from its newest checkpoint with it and running that round; the judge approves the release only after it. The tuner writes the kept worker's two worker.json files with `worker show` (passing `worker check`) into its release with what it changed. There is no pull request to HuTian-Workers in this round; that comes after the last round.

Every world you run: the full configuration of the world it continues with only the worker of paper-repo and internal-review-repo changed, and "resources": [] written out; budget.total_seconds 1800, at most 12 turns and 1800 model seconds. Note from the last world: a verifier batch once hung in the judge's sandbox (pymupdf loads onnxruntime, whose thread affinity fails under the sandbox's CPU set); the world ends such a turn, and a run can be retried. This world ends at its wall-clock budget; have the release done well before it.

Comparison and decision: run the incumbent and each candidate at least five times each on the held-out paper, all from c0 of rw_19be25bd2f7d and all at the same time, judged as the protocol says (verifier reward with every component, and the blind rubric). Keep a candidate only if both hold on the held-out paper: its blind writing-quality score is above the incumbent's by more than the spread of the runs, and its verifier reward is not below the incumbent's. If no candidate passes, make a new round of at most two candidates from what the judging shows, and compare again, until one passes or this world's wall clock runs out; at least one candidate in every round changes writing content through assets, and one that changes only effort says so.

Put back and publish, as before: put the kept worker back by continuing rw_313df9cf84a4 from its newest checkpoint with it and running that round; the judge approves the release only after it. Publish the kept worker to a-green-hand-jack/HuTian-Workers by a pull request through the github resource: its worker.json written by `worker show` and passing `worker check`, beside a README.md that says what it changed against incumbent@v3 and by how much on which measures (writing quality and each verifier component, with the spread); if the incumbent is kept, the README says why and on which measures the difference stayed within the spread.

Every world you run: the full configuration of the world it continues with only the worker of paper-repo and internal-review-repo changed, and "resources": [] written out (a world made here without it gets this world's resources, the held-out material among them); budget.total_seconds 1800, at most 12 turns and 1800 model seconds. This world ends at its wall-clock budget; have the release and the pull request done well before it.

issue.author: ht-admin
issue.body:
Improve the paper-writing worker of the positions paper-repo and internal-review-repo of the research world rw_313df9cf84a4, given to you to read. It is a writing-only world made from PaperWrite-Bench task paper_29 (write a 10-page ICLR 2025 paper from the supplied overview, figures, tables and bibliography, into workspace/submission/manuscript.tex and manuscript.pdf; no experiments, no internet). Both incumbents are a-green-hand-jack/HuTian-Workers:incumbent@v3 (Claude Code, claude-sonnet-5-5, effort low). The goal is a worker that really writes better papers, not one that writes this paper better.

What is already measured: the incumbent ran three times on paper_29 from the checkpoint c0 of rw_313df9cf84a4 (c0 is that world before any turn): rw_313df9cf84a4 itself and rw_ec90a7b1da48, rw_017cc0de3d32 (the same state root). Each took about 3.5 minutes, one writing turn and one review that approved at once; a single Claude Code with the same model and effort, without positions, took the same time. The benchmark's verifier gave 0.794, 0.820 and 0.805 (26, 42 and 33 of the 149 references cited). The verifier and the files to run it are in your inputs (verifier/README.md); it measures form and citation coverage, not writing quality.

Training and held-out: paper_29 is for training: diagnosis and candidates are made from it. The held-out paper is PaperWrite-Bench paper_39 (ACL 2025), the world rw_557d19f77f34 given to you to read, checkpoint c0, never run. It belongs to the task-setter and the judge alone: the task-setter keeps its tasks in its repository files and the judge runs them; the tuner and the diagnostician do not read rw_557d19f77f34, its verifier files, or any world made from it.

Judging: the judge scores every manuscript (1) with the verifier, recording the reward and every component, and (2) for writing quality with a rubric the task-setter writes and the judge applies the same way to every manuscript, blind to which worker wrote it (label the manuscripts at random before reading, unblind after scoring). The rubric says that citing references for coverage rather than for what the text says (dumping the bibliography) is recognised and penalised; a gain in citation coverage counts only where the citations fit their context.

Candidates: at most two in a round, each Claude Code with claude-sonnet-5-5, changing the worker's content: files in its assets (writing norms or a skill: structure, use of citations, a self-check list), Claude Code's native settings, or effort. At least one candidate changes writing content through assets, not only effort; a candidate that changes only effort says so in its record.

Comparison and decision: run the incumbent and each candidate three times each on the held-out paper, all from c0 of rw_557d19f77f34 and all at the same time. Keep a candidate only if both hold on the held-out paper: its blind writing-quality score is above the incumbent's by more than the spread of the runs, and its verifier reward is not below the incumbent's. Held-out tasks on paper_29 material may be added as a supplement; the decision rests on paper_39. If no candidate passes and time is left, make another round of candidates.

Put back and publish: put the kept worker back by continuing rw_313df9cf84a4 from its newest checkpoint with it and running that round; the judge approves the release only after it. Publish the kept worker to a-green-hand-jack/HuTian-Workers by a pull request through the github resource: its worker.json written by `worker show` and passing `worker check`, beside a README.md that says what it changed against incumbent@v3 and by how much on which measures (writing quality and each verifier component, with the spread); if the incumbent is kept, the README says why and on which measures the difference stayed within the spread.

Every world you run: the configuration of the world it continues with only the worker of paper-repo and internal-review-repo changed (resources stay empty as there), budget.total_seconds 1800, at most 12 turns and 1800 model seconds. This world itself ends at its wall-clock budget; plan to have the release and the pull request done well before it.

issue.body:
Round 2. This world continues the round-1 world dw_ae1c3437dfc5 and starts the second round of training the paper-writing worker of paper-repo and internal-review-repo; the model stays Claude Code claude-sonnet-5-5, only the workers' content and settings change.

Where round 1 ended. The incumbent is cand-a (the tuner's final/cand-a-writer/v1 and final/cand-a-reviewer/v1, from the put-back world rw_3bd589d0ab01). Round 1's rubric record (the judge's evaluation/round-3-evaluation.json and round-3-summary.md at dbd60a1) does not count: its rubric scores were written into a script as fixed vectors per world id, grouped under the worker names, and its labels were drawn after the scores, so no manuscript was read blind. Its verifier results stand (evaluation/verifier-h1-v2/: incumbent@v3 0.883, cand-a 0.905, cand-c 0.750, cand-d 0.750), and so does its decision: cand-c and cand-d cannot be kept, since their verifier means are below cand-a's whatever their rubric scores. Rubric v2 (the task-setter's release rubric-v2, sha256 5df317ee3a2b8b49d785f7f7b4195d1b5a49337f939cab25dde4ff0e720f1250) and the decision rule are unchanged.

This round, in order:
1. Diagnose cand-a from its runs on the diagnostic tasks and round 1's verifier results (not round 1's rubric record), and make one candidate from the diagnosis, changing only the two workers' content and settings. Write what it changes and why.
2. The position that keeps the held-out tasks, which does not score, runs the held-out paper for cand-a and for the candidate, five times each, all at once: each run continued from c0 of rw_19be25bd2f7d with the full configuration of that world, only the worker of paper-repo and internal-review-repo changed, "resources": [] written out, budget.total_seconds 1800, at most 12 turns and 1800 model seconds.
3. The same position makes the scoring package of 20 manuscripts: those 10 runs, and round 1's counted runs of incumbent@v3 (rw_2b870195a2d4, rw_a0e901375c45, rw_12fbeddbaad5, rw_708decbf1039, rw_6be99cce051e) and of cand-a (rw_9175d31098ad, rw_26876f95e540, rw_9a621cb36ad3, rw_2bf3286ecd76, rw_220c411c77b7), which are in the root given you to read that ends in dw_59f01b2fe95e/worlds/judge. It copies each manuscript (manuscript.tex, manuscript.pdf and what the verifier needs, nothing that names the world or the worker) into a directory named by a random label it draws, and pushes the package for the judge together with the sha256 of the table that maps each label to its world and worker. The table itself stays out of every repository, issue and comment until the judge has pushed all 20 scores; then this position pushes it, and it must match the sha256.
4. The judge scores the package blind with rubric v2. Until the table is published it uses only the package: no export, `config show`, `status` or `monitor` of a held-out world, no comparison of package files with other files, and none of round 1's manuscripts already in its repository. For each manuscript and each of the 12 items it writes the score (0–4), one sentence of reason, and a quotation of at most 30 words from that manuscript with its section or page. Every score comes from reading that manuscript; a script may collect scores already written per manuscript, never produce them. This may take several turns: push after every five manuscripts scored; a manuscript not yet read has no score. It runs the verifier on each package manuscript, one at a time, and records reward and every component.
5. When the table is published, the judge unblinds and writes the round summary: for each group (incumbent@v3 of round 1, cand-a of round 1, cand-a of this round, the candidate): v2 mean, min, max, spread and each item's mean; verifier mean, min, max and each component. It applies the rule against cand-a's runs of this round: the candidate is kept only if its v2 mean is above cand-a's by more than cand-a's spread (max minus min) and its verifier mean is not below cand-a's. It pushes the summary and the decision.
6. The position that puts the kept worker back continues rw_313df9cf84a4 from its newest checkpoint with the kept worker and runs that round now; put-backs of earlier rounds do not count.
7. The tuner writes the kept worker's two worker.json files with `worker show` from this round's put-back world, passing `worker check`, with what changed (if cand-a is kept, its version stays).
8. The judge approves the release only after 5, 6 and 7, and its approval names the summary (its commit) and this round's put-back world.

Who reads what: the held-out worlds (rw_19be25bd2f7d and every world made from it), the heldout-material resource, the paper_39 verifier files, the held-out manuscripts and the package belong to the position that keeps the held-out tasks and to the judge alone; after the decision is pushed, the positions that diagnose and change the worker may read the summary, not the manuscripts. No pull request to HuTian-Workers in this round. This world ends at its wall-clock budget; have the release done well before it.

5. The judge approves the release only after 2, 3 and 4, and says in its approval which summary and which put-back world it relies on.

Who reads what is as before: the held-out worlds (rw_19be25bd2f7d, the 29 runs and every world made from them), the heldout-material resource, the paper_39 verifier files and the held-out manuscripts belong to the task-setter and the judge alone; after the decision is pushed, the diagnostician and the tuner may read the summary, not the manuscripts. issue.author: ht-admin
issue.body:
Round 1 of at least three on the paper-writing worker of the positions paper-repo and internal-review-repo of the research world rw_313df9cf84a4 (PaperWrite-Bench paper_29, given to you to read). The aim over the rounds is a curve: each round's kept worker writes better than the last. This world is one round: one diagnosis, at most two candidates, one comparison, one decision.

Where we start. The last world kept cand-a, now published and merged in a-green-hand-jack/HuTian-Workers as cand-a-writer@v1 (paper-repo) and cand-a-reviewer@v1 (internal-review-repo): incumbent@v3 (Claude Code, claude-sonnet-5-5, effort low) plus a CLAUDE.md of writing and review norms. On the held-out paper it raised the blind score from 26.4 to 30.8 of 32 and the verifier reward from 0.886 to 0.900, but it writes longer papers (11 pages in 2 of 5 runs against the 9-page target) and its section_score fell from 0.96 to 0.88. cand-a is the incumbent of this round; the original incumbent@v3 is the curve's origin.

The rubric first. The 32-point rubric can no longer decide: cand-a's mean 30.8 plus its spread 2.0 is above the maximum, so no candidate could ever pass. Before anyone looks at a manuscript made in this world, the task-setter writes rubric v2 with room above cand-a. Its items and the levels of each item come from what the task and the benchmark ask of a paper: the page limit and venue in each task's metadata and template, the required sections the task instruction lists (abstract, introduction, related work, method, experiments, limitations, conclusion), the template's format kept, every claim grounded in the supplied overview, the supplied figures and tables used and interpreted, citations from the given bibliography that fit their sentences; plus how well the paper argues and reads. Every level has an anchored description so two judges would give the same score. It must apply unchanged to any PaperWrite-Bench paper (numbers such as the page limit are read from each task), not only paper_29 or paper_39, and it must not be shaped around cand-a's weaknesses. Freeze it: put it in the task-setter's release with its sha256, and do not change it in this or any later round. Scores under the old rubric stay as they are, for the record.

Diagnosis. The sparring-partner runs the incumbent cand-a twice on the training paper, continuing rw_313df9cf84a4 from c0, for the diagnostician; the diagnostician diagnoses what cand-a still does badly in writing, from those runs, from the earlier paper_29 runs, and from the judge's summary of the last world's comparison (aggregate scores per worker and item, no held-out manuscripts). The tuner makes at most two candidates from the diagnosis, each starting from cand-a: only the worker's content and settings change (assets, instructions, effort and other settings of Claude Code); the agent and the model stay Claude Code and claude-sonnet-5-5; at least one candidate changes writing content through assets, and one that changes only a setting says so. Nothing in a candidate may be about a particular paper.

Comparison and decision. The judge runs, from c0 of rw_19be25bd2f7d (paper_39, ACL 2025) and all at the same time, five runs each of incumbent@v3, cand-a and every candidate: twenty worlds with two candidates. If the provider answers with overloads or the host refuses, start them in two batches with the same mix of workers and say so. Judge every manuscript with the frozen rubric v2, blind (random labels before reading, unblinded after all are scored), and with the verifier (reward and every component), as before. Keep a candidate only if its blind mean under v2 is above cand-a's mean by more than cand-a's spread (max minus min of its runs) and its verifier mean is not below cand-a's; if both pass, keep the better and say why; if none passes, cand-a stays and the record says on which measures the difference stayed within the spread. Record for every worker the v2 blind mean, min, max and spread, the mean of each item, and the verifier mean, min, max and every component, in a round summary in the judge's repository. After the decision is recorded, the diagnostician and the tuner may read that summary for the next round, but not the manuscripts.

Who reads what. rw_19be25bd2f7d, every world made from it, the heldout-material resource, the paper_39 verifier files in your inputs and the held-out manuscripts belong to the task-setter and the judge alone: the sparring-partner, the tuner and the diagnostician do not read any of them.

Put back. The sparring-partner puts the kept worker back by continuing rw_313df9cf84a4 from its newest checkpoint with it and running that round; the judge approves the release only after it. The tuner writes the kept worker's two worker.json files with `worker show` (passing `worker check`) into its release with what it changed. There is no pull request to HuTian-Workers in this round; that comes after the last round.

Every world you run: the full configuration of the world it continues with only the worker of paper-repo and internal-review-repo changed, and "resources": [] written out; budget.total_seconds 1800, at most 12 turns and 1800 model seconds. Note from the last world: a verifier batch once hung in the judge's sandbox (pymupdf loads onnxruntime, whose thread affinity fails under the sandbox's CPU set); the world ends such a turn, and a run can be retried. This world ends at its wall-clock budget; have the release done well before it.

issue.author: ht-admin
issue.body:
Second round on the paper-writing worker of the positions paper-repo and internal-review-repo of the research world rw_313df9cf84a4 (PaperWrite-Bench paper_29, given to you to read), starting from what the first round delivered: the diagnosis, the rubric and the held-out protocol, and the candidates cand-a and cand-b (a CLAUDE.md asset with writing and review norms; cand-b also at higher effort), whose paper_29 runs scored 0.79-0.82, within the incumbent's range. The incumbent is still a-green-hand-jack/HuTian-Workers:incumbent@v3 (Claude Code, claude-sonnet-5-5, effort low). The goal is a worker that really writes better papers; keeping the incumbent is a result only if no candidate wins before this world's wall clock ends.

The held-out world changed: rw_557d19f77f34 could not be continued from c0 (a world problem, recorded and fixed apart from this world). Its replacement is rw_19be25bd2f7d, the same paper_39 (ACL 2025) task, given to you to read, checkpoint c0, never run; continuing it from c0 was checked. The held-out paper's writing material, exactly what the benchmark gives its writers, is now the resource heldout-material (paper_39/), so the judge can check every manuscript's numbers and claims against the source. rw_19be25bd2f7d, the heldout-material resource, the verifier files of paper_39 and every world made from rw_19be25bd2f7d belong to the task-setter and the judge alone: the judge runs the held-out worlds itself, and the sparring-partner, the tuner and the diagnostician do not read any of them.

Comparison and decision: run the incumbent and each candidate at least five times each on the held-out paper, all from c0 of rw_19be25bd2f7d and all at the same time, judged as the protocol says (verifier reward with every component, and the blind rubric). Keep a candidate only if both hold on the held-out paper: its blind writing-quality score is above the incumbent's by more than the spread of the runs, and its verifier reward is not below the incumbent's. If no candidate passes, make a new round of at most two candidates from what the judging shows, and compare again, until one passes or this world's wall clock runs out; at least one candidate in every round changes writing content through assets, and one that changes only effort says so.

Put back and publish, as before: put the kept worker back by continuing rw_313df9cf84a4 from its newest checkpoint with it and running that round; the judge approves the release only after it. Publish the kept worker to a-green-hand-jack/HuTian-Workers by a pull request through the github resource: its worker.json written by `worker show` and passing `worker check`, beside a README.md that says what it changed against incumbent@v3 and by how much on which measures (writing quality and each verifier component, with the spread); if the incumbent is kept, the README says why and on which measures the difference stayed within the spread.

Every world you run: the full configuration of the world it continues with only the worker of paper-repo and internal-review-repo changed, and "resources": [] written out (a world made here without it gets this world's resources, the held-out material among them); budget.total_seconds 1800, at most 12 turns and 1800 model seconds. This world ends at its wall-clock budget; have the release and the pull request done well before it.

issue.author: ht-admin
issue.body:
Improve the paper-writing worker of the positions paper-repo and internal-review-repo of the research world rw_313df9cf84a4, given to you to read. It is a writing-only world made from PaperWrite-Bench task paper_29 (write a 10-page ICLR 2025 paper from the supplied overview, figures, tables and bibliography, into workspace/submission/manuscript.tex and manuscript.pdf; no experiments, no internet). Both incumbents are a-green-hand-jack/HuTian-Workers:incumbent@v3 (Claude Code, claude-sonnet-5-5, effort low). The goal is a worker that really writes better papers, not one that writes this paper better.

What is already measured: the incumbent ran three times on paper_29 from the checkpoint c0 of rw_313df9cf84a4 (c0 is that world before any turn): rw_313df9cf84a4 itself and rw_ec90a7b1da48, rw_017cc0de3d32 (the same state root). Each took about 3.5 minutes, one writing turn and one review that approved at once; a single Claude Code with the same model and effort, without positions, took the same time. The benchmark's verifier gave 0.794, 0.820 and 0.805 (26, 42 and 33 of the 149 references cited). The verifier and the files to run it are in your inputs (verifier/README.md); it measures form and citation coverage, not writing quality.

Training and held-out: paper_29 is for training: diagnosis and candidates are made from it. The held-out paper is PaperWrite-Bench paper_39 (ACL 2025), the world rw_557d19f77f34 given to you to read, checkpoint c0, never run. It belongs to the task-setter and the judge alone: the task-setter keeps its tasks in its repository files and the judge runs them; the tuner and the diagnostician do not read rw_557d19f77f34, its verifier files, or any world made from it.

Judging: the judge scores every manuscript (1) with the verifier, recording the reward and every component, and (2) for writing quality with a rubric the task-setter writes and the judge applies the same way to every manuscript, blind to which worker wrote it (label the manuscripts at random before reading, unblind after scoring). The rubric says that citing references for coverage rather than for what the text says (dumping the bibliography) is recognised and penalised; a gain in citation coverage counts only where the citations fit their context.

Candidates: at most two in a round, each Claude Code with claude-sonnet-5-5, changing the worker's content: files in its assets (writing norms or a skill: structure, use of citations, a self-check list), Claude Code's native settings, or effort. At least one candidate changes writing content through assets, not only effort; a candidate that changes only effort says so in its record.

Comparison and decision: run the incumbent and each candidate three times each on the held-out paper, all from c0 of rw_557d19f77f34 and all at the same time. Keep a candidate only if both hold on the held-out paper: its blind writing-quality score is above the incumbent's by more than the spread of the runs, and its verifier reward is not below the incumbent's. Held-out tasks on paper_29 material may be added as a supplement; the decision rests on paper_39. If no candidate passes and time is left, make another round of candidates.

Put back and publish: put the kept worker back by continuing rw_313df9cf84a4 from its newest checkpoint with it and running that round; the judge approves the release only after it. Publish the kept worker to a-green-hand-jack/HuTian-Workers by a pull request through the github resource: its worker.json written by `worker show` and passing `worker check`, beside a README.md that says what it changed against incumbent@v3 and by how much on which measures (writing quality and each verifier component, with the spread); if the incumbent is kept, the README says why and on which measures the difference stayed within the spread.

Every world you run: the configuration of the world it continues with only the worker of paper-repo and internal-review-repo changed (resources stay empty as there), budget.total_seconds 1800, at most 12 turns and 1800 model seconds. This world itself ends at its wall-clock budget; plan to have the release and the pull request done well before it.

issue.author: ht-admin
issue.body:
Round 1 of at least three on the paper-writing worker of the positions paper-repo and internal-review-repo of the research world rw_313df9cf84a4 (PaperWrite-Bench paper_29, given to you to read). The aim over the rounds is a curve: each round's kept worker writes better than the last. This world is one round: one diagnosis, at most two candidates, one comparison, one decision.

Where we start. The last world kept cand-a, now published and merged in a-green-hand-jack/HuTian-Workers as cand-a-writer@v1 (paper-repo) and cand-a-reviewer@v1 (internal-review-repo): incumbent@v3 (Claude Code, claude-sonnet-5-5, effort low) plus a CLAUDE.md of writing and review norms. On the held-out paper it raised the blind score from 26.4 to 30.8 of 32 and the verifier reward from 0.886 to 0.900, but it writes longer papers (11 pages in 2 of 5 runs against the 9-page target) and its section_score fell from 0.96 to 0.88. cand-a is the incumbent of this round; the original incumbent@v3 is the curve's origin.

The rubric first. The 32-point rubric can no longer decide: cand-a's mean 30.8 plus its spread 2.0 is above the maximum, so no candidate could ever pass. Before anyone looks at a manuscript made in this world, the task-setter writes rubric v2 with room above cand-a. Its items and the levels of each item come from what the task and the benchmark ask of a paper: the page limit and venue in each task's metadata and template, the required sections the task instruction lists (abstract, introduction, related work, method, experiments, limitations, conclusion), the template's format kept, every claim grounded in the supplied overview, the supplied figures and tables used and interpreted, citations from the given bibliography that fit their sentences; plus how well the paper argues and reads. Every level has an anchored description so two judges would give the same score. It must apply unchanged to any PaperWrite-Bench paper (numbers such as the page limit are read from each task), not only paper_29 or paper_39, and it must not be shaped around cand-a's weaknesses. Freeze it: put it in the task-setter's release with its sha256, and do not change it in this or any later round. Scores under the old rubric stay as they are, for the record.

Diagnosis. The sparring-partner runs the incumbent cand-a twice on the training paper, continuing rw_313df9cf84a4 from c0, for the diagnostician; the diagnostician diagnoses what cand-a still does badly in writing, from those runs, from the earlier paper_29 runs, and from the judge's summary of the last world's comparison (aggregate scores per worker and item, no held-out manuscripts). The tuner makes at most two candidates from the diagnosis, each starting from cand-a: only the worker's content and settings change (assets, instructions, effort and other settings of Claude Code); the agent and the model stay Claude Code and claude-sonnet-5-5; at least one candidate changes writing content through assets, and one that changes only a setting says so. Nothing in a candidate may be about a particular paper.

Comparison and decision. The judge runs, from c0 of rw_19be25bd2f7d (paper_39, ACL 2025) and all at the same time, five runs each of incumbent@v3, cand-a and every candidate: twenty worlds with two candidates. If the provider answers with overloads or the host refuses, start them in two batches with the same mix of workers and say so. Judge every manuscript with the frozen rubric v2, blind (random labels before reading, unblinded after all are scored), and with the verifier (reward and every component), as before. Keep a candidate only if its blind mean under v2 is above cand-a's mean by more than cand-a's spread (max minus min of its runs) and its verifier mean is not below cand-a's; if both pass, keep the better and say why; if none passes, cand-a stays and the record says on which measures the difference stayed within the spread. Record for every worker the v2 blind mean, min, max and spread, the mean of each item, and the verifier mean, min, max and every component, in a round summary in the judge's repository. After the decision is recorded, the diagnostician and the tuner may read that summary for the next round, but not the manuscripts.

Who reads what. rw_19be25bd2f7d, every world made from it, the heldout-material resource, the paper_39 verifier files in your inputs and the held-out manuscripts belong to the task-setter and the judge alone: the sparring-partner, the tuner and the diagnostician do not read any of them.

Put back. The sparring-partner puts the kept worker back by continuing rw_313df9cf84a4 from its newest checkpoint with it and running that round; the judge approves the release only after it. The tuner writes the kept worker's two worker.json files with `worker show` (passing `worker check`) into its release with what it changed. There is no pull request to HuTian-Workers in this round; that comes after the last round.

Every world you run: the full configuration of the world it continues with only the worker of paper-repo and internal-review-repo changed, and "resources": [] written out; budget.total_seconds 1800, at most 12 turns and 1800 model seconds. Note from the last world: a verifier batch once hung in the judge's sandbox (pymupdf loads onnxruntime, whose thread affinity fails under the sandbox's CPU set); the world ends such a turn, and a run can be retried. This world ends at its wall-clock budget; have the release done well before it.

issue.author: ht-admin
issue.body:
Improve the paper-writing worker of the positions paper-repo and internal-review-repo of the research world rw_313df9cf84a4, given to you to read. It is a writing-only world made from PaperWrite-Bench task paper_29 (write a 10-page ICLR 2025 paper from the supplied overview, figures, tables and bibliography, into workspace/submission/manuscript.tex and manuscript.pdf; no experiments, no internet). Both incumbents are a-green-hand-jack/HuTian-Workers:incumbent@v3 (Claude Code, claude-sonnet-5-5, effort low). The goal is a worker that really writes better papers, not one that writes this paper better.

What is already measured: the incumbent ran three times on paper_29 from the checkpoint c0 of rw_313df9cf84a4 (c0 is that world before any turn): rw_313df9cf84a4 itself and rw_ec90a7b1da48, rw_017cc0de3d32 (the same state root). Each took about 3.5 minutes, one writing turn and one review that approved at once; a single Claude Code with the same model and effort, without positions, took the same time. The benchmark's verifier gave 0.794, 0.820 and 0.805 (26, 42 and 33 of the 149 references cited). The verifier and the files to run it are in your inputs (verifier/README.md); it measures form and citation coverage, not writing quality.

Training and held-out: paper_29 is for training: diagnosis and candidates are made from it. The held-out paper is PaperWrite-Bench paper_39 (ACL 2025), the world rw_557d19f77f34 given to you to read, checkpoint c0, never run. It belongs to the task-setter and the judge alone: the task-setter keeps its tasks in its repository files and the judge runs them; the tuner and the diagnostician do not read rw_557d19f77f34, its verifier files, or any world made from it.

Judging: the judge scores every manuscript (1) with the verifier, recording the reward and every component, and (2) for writing quality with a rubric the task-setter writes and the judge applies the same way to every manuscript, blind to which worker wrote it (label the manuscripts at random before reading, unblind after scoring). The rubric says that citing references for coverage rather than for what the text says (dumping the bibliography) is recognised and penalised; a gain in citation coverage counts only where the citations fit their context.

Candidates: at most two in a round, each Claude Code with claude-sonnet-5-5, changing the worker's content: files in its assets (writing norms or a skill: structure, use of citations, a self-check list), Claude Code's native settings, or effort. At least one candidate changes writing content through assets, not only effort; a candidate that changes only effort says so in its record.

Comparison and decision: run the incumbent and each candidate three times each on the held-out paper, all from c0 of rw_557d19f77f34 and all at the same time. Keep a candidate only if both hold on the held-out paper: its blind writing-quality score is above the incumbent's by more than the spread of the runs, and its verifier reward is not below the incumbent's. Held-out tasks on paper_29 material may be added as a supplement; the decision rests on paper_39. If no candidate passes and time is left, make another round of candidates.

Put back and publish: put the kept worker back by continuing rw_313df9cf84a4 from its newest checkpoint with it and running that round; the judge approves the release only after it. Publish the kept worker to a-green-hand-jack/HuTian-Workers by a pull request through the github resource: its worker.json written by `worker show` and passing `worker check`, beside a README.md that says what it changed against incumbent@v3 and by how much on which measures (writing quality and each verifier component, with the spread); if the incumbent is kept, the README says why and on which measures the difference stayed within the spread.

Every world you run: the configuration of the world it continues with only the worker of paper-repo and internal-review-repo changed (resources stay empty as there), budget.total_seconds 1800, at most 12 turns and 1800 model seconds. This world itself ends at its wall-clock budget; plan to have the release and the pull request done well before it.

issue.author: ht-admin
issue.body:
Round 2. This world continues the round-1 world dw_ae1c3437dfc5 and starts the second round of training the paper-writing worker of paper-repo and internal-review-repo; the model stays Claude Code claude-sonnet-5-5, only the workers' content and settings change.

Where round 1 ended. The incumbent is cand-a (the tuner's final/cand-a-writer/v1 and final/cand-a-reviewer/v1, from the put-back world rw_3bd589d0ab01). Round 1's rubric record (the judge's evaluation/round-3-evaluation.json and round-3-summary.md at dbd60a1) does not count: its rubric scores were written into a script as fixed vectors per world id, grouped under the worker names, and its labels were drawn after the scores, so no manuscript was read blind. Its verifier results stand (evaluation/verifier-h1-v2/: incumbent@v3 0.883, cand-a 0.905, cand-c 0.750, cand-d 0.750), and so does its decision: cand-c and cand-d cannot be kept, since their verifier means are below cand-a's whatever their rubric scores. Rubric v2 (the task-setter's release rubric-v2, sha256 5df317ee3a2b8b49d785f7f7b4195d1b5a49337f939cab25dde4ff0e720f1250) and the decision rule are unchanged.

This round, in order:
1. Diagnose cand-a from its runs on the diagnostic tasks and round 1's verifier results (not round 1's rubric record), and make one candidate from the diagnosis, changing only the two workers' content and settings. Write what it changes and why.
2. The position that keeps the held-out tasks, which does not score, runs the held-out paper for cand-a and for the candidate, five times each, all at once: each run continued from c0 of rw_19be25bd2f7d with the full configuration of that world, only the worker of paper-repo and internal-review-repo changed, "resources": [] written out, budget.total_seconds 1800, at most 12 turns and 1800 model seconds.
3. The same position makes the scoring package of 20 manuscripts: those 10 runs, and round 1's counted runs of incumbent@v3 (rw_2b870195a2d4, rw_a0e901375c45, rw_12fbeddbaad5, rw_708decbf1039, rw_6be99cce051e) and of cand-a (rw_9175d31098ad, rw_26876f95e540, rw_9a621cb36ad3, rw_2bf3286ecd76, rw_220c411c77b7), which are in the root given you to read that ends in dw_59f01b2fe95e/worlds/judge. It copies each manuscript (manuscript.tex, manuscript.pdf and what the verifier needs, nothing that names the world or the worker) into a directory named by a random label it draws, and pushes the package for the judge together with the sha256 of the table that maps each label to its world and worker. The table itself stays out of every repository, issue and comment until the judge has pushed all 20 scores; then this position pushes it, and it must match the sha256.
4. The judge scores the package blind with rubric v2. Until the table is published it uses only the package: no export, `config show`, `status` or `monitor` of a held-out world, no comparison of package files with other files, and none of round 1's manuscripts already in its repository. For each manuscript and each of the 12 items it writes the score (0–4), one sentence of reason, and a quotation of at most 30 words from that manuscript with its section or page. Every score comes from reading that manuscript; a script may collect scores already written per manuscript, never produce them. This may take several turns: push after every five manuscripts scored; a manuscript not yet read has no score. It runs the verifier on each package manuscript, one at a time, and records reward and every component.
5. When the table is published, the judge unblinds and writes the round summary: for each group (incumbent@v3 of round 1, cand-a of round 1, cand-a of this round, the candidate): v2 mean, min, max, spread and each item's mean; verifier mean, min, max and each component. It applies the rule against cand-a's runs of this round: the candidate is kept only if its v2 mean is above cand-a's by more than cand-a's spread (max minus min) and its verifier mean is not below cand-a's. It pushes the summary and the decision.
6. The position that puts the kept worker back continues rw_313df9cf84a4 from its newest checkpoint with the kept worker and runs that round now; put-backs of earlier rounds do not count.
7. The tuner writes the kept worker's two worker.json files with `worker show` from this round's put-back world, passing `worker check`, with what changed (if cand-a is kept, its version stays).
8. The judge approves the release only after 5, 6 and 7, and its approval names the summary (its commit) and this round's put-back world.

Who reads what: the held-out worlds (rw_19be25bd2f7d and every world made from it), the heldout-material resource, the paper_39 verifier files, the held-out manuscripts and the package belong to the position that keeps the held-out tasks and to the judge alone; after the decision is pushed, the positions that diagnose and change the worker may read the summary, not the manuscripts. No pull request to HuTian-Workers in this round. This world ends at its wall-clock budget; have the release done well before it.

issue.author: ht-admin
issue.body:
Round 1, completed. This world continues the round-1 world dw_59f01b2fe95e, whose objective stands unchanged (rubric v2, cand-a as the incumbent, cand-c and cand-d, the comparison, the decision, the put-back). That world ended before its round was done: the judge approved its release before any held-out manuscript was scored and before this round's put-back, taking the put-back of the world before (rw_b555f821ee2b in the sparring-partner's runs/putback-cand-a, made with cand-a in the previous round) for this round's. Nothing of this round was decided.

What is done and stays: rubric v2 is frozen in the task-setter's release rubric-v2 (sha256 5df317ee3a2b8b49d785f7f7b4195d1b5a49337f939cab25dde4ff0e720f1250) and is used as it is; the diagnosis of cand-a and the candidates cand-c and cand-d (tuner, CANDIDATES.md) stand; the held-out runs are finished. They are the 29 worlds in the root given you to read that ends in dw_59f01b2fe95e/worlds/judge, all continued from c0 of rw_19be25bd2f7d and all released; `config show` names each one's worker (incumbent@v3, or the assets and effort of cand-a, cand-c or cand-d). Do not run the held-out paper again.

What is left, in order:
1. The judge assigns every one of the 29 worlds to its worker from its configuration. For a worker with more than five runs, the five created first are scored and the others are not counted. Before reading any manuscript, the judge writes this rule, the assignment of all 29 worlds with their creation times, and the list of the runs not counted (world id, worker, why) into its repository and pushes it.
2. The judge scores those manuscripts blind with rubric v2 (random labels before reading, unblinded after all are scored) and runs the verifier on each (reward and every component), then applies the rule against cand-a: a candidate is kept only if its v2 blind mean is above cand-a's mean by more than cand-a's spread (max minus min) and its verifier mean is not below cand-a's. It writes the round summary (for every worker: v2 mean, min, max, spread, each item's mean; verifier mean, min, max and each component) in its repository and pushes it.
3. The sparring-partner puts the kept worker back by continuing rw_313df9cf84a4 from its newest checkpoint with it and running that round now; the put-back of the previous world does not count.
4. The tuner writes the kept worker's two worker.json files with `worker show` from the put-back world, passing `worker check`, with what it changed.
5. The judge approves the release only after 2, 3 and 4, and says in its approval which summary and which put-back world it relies on.

Who reads what is as before: the held-out worlds (rw_19be25bd2f7d, the 29 runs and every world made from them), the heldout-material resource, the paper_39 verifier files and the held-out manuscripts belong to the task-setter and the judge alone; after the decision is pushed, the diagnostician and the tuner may read the summary, not the manuscripts. No pull request to HuTian-Workers in this round. Every world you run: the full configuration of the world it continues with only the worker of paper-repo and internal-review-repo changed, "resources": [] written out, budget.total_seconds 1800, at most 12 turns and 1800 model seconds. This world ends at its wall-clock budget; have the release done well before it.

issue.author: ht-admin
issue.body:
Round 1 of at least three on the paper-writing worker of the positions paper-repo and internal-review-repo of the research world rw_313df9cf84a4 (PaperWrite-Bench paper_29, given to you to read). The aim over the rounds is a curve: each round's kept worker writes better than the last. This world is one round: one diagnosis, at most two candidates, one comparison, one decision.

Where we start. The last world kept cand-a, now published and merged in a-green-hand-jack/HuTian-Workers as cand-a-writer@v1 (paper-repo) and cand-a-reviewer@v1 (internal-review-repo): incumbent@v3 (Claude Code, claude-sonnet-5-5, effort low) plus a CLAUDE.md of writing and review norms. On the held-out paper it raised the blind score from 26.4 to 30.8 of 32 and the verifier reward from 0.886 to 0.900, but it writes longer papers (11 pages in 2 of 5 runs against the 9-page target) and its section_score fell from 0.96 to 0.88. cand-a is the incumbent of this round; the original incumbent@v3 is the curve's origin.

The rubric first. The 32-point rubric can no longer decide: cand-a's mean 30.8 plus its spread 2.0 is above the maximum, so no candidate could ever pass. Before anyone looks at a manuscript made in this world, the task-setter writes rubric v2 with room above cand-a. Its items and the levels of each item come from what the task and the benchmark ask of a paper: the page limit and venue in each task's metadata and template, the required sections the task instruction lists (abstract, introduction, related work, method, experiments, limitations, conclusion), the template's format kept, every claim grounded in the supplied overview, the supplied figures and tables used and interpreted, citations from the given bibliography that fit their sentences; plus how well the paper argues and reads. Every level has an anchored description so two judges would give the same score. It must apply unchanged to any PaperWrite-Bench paper (numbers such as the page limit are read from each task), not only paper_29 or paper_39, and it must not be shaped around cand-a's weaknesses. Freeze it: put it in the task-setter's release with its sha256, and do not change it in this or any later round. Scores under the old rubric stay as they are, for the record.

Diagnosis. The sparring-partner runs the incumbent cand-a twice on the training paper, continuing rw_313df9cf84a4 from c0, for the diagnostician; the diagnostician diagnoses what cand-a still does badly in writing, from those runs, from the earlier paper_29 runs, and from the judge's summary of the last world's comparison (aggregate scores per worker and item, no held-out manuscripts). The tuner makes at most two candidates from the diagnosis, each starting from cand-a: only the worker's content and settings change (assets, instructions, effort and other settings of Claude Code); the agent and the model stay Claude Code and claude-sonnet-5-5; at least one candidate changes writing content through assets, and one that changes only a setting says so. Nothing in a candidate may be about a particular paper.

Comparison and decision. The judge runs, from c0 of rw_19be25bd2f7d (paper_39, ACL 2025) and all at the same time, five runs each of incumbent@v3, cand-a and every candidate: twenty worlds with two candidates. If the provider answers with overloads or the host refuses, start them in two batches with the same mix of workers and say so. Judge every manuscript with the frozen rubric v2, blind (random labels before reading, unblinded after all are scored), and with the verifier (reward and every component), as before. Keep a candidate only if its blind mean under v2 is above cand-a's mean by more than cand-a's spread (max minus min of its runs) and its verifier mean is not below cand-a's; if both pass, keep the better and say why; if none passes, cand-a stays and the record says on which measures the difference stayed within the spread. Record for every worker the v2 blind mean, min, max and spread, the mean of each item, and the verifier mean, min, max and every component, in a round summary in the judge's repository. After the decision is recorded, the diagnostician and the tuner may read that summary for the next round, but not the manuscripts.

Who reads what. rw_19be25bd2f7d, every world made from it, the heldout-material resource, the paper_39 verifier files in your inputs and the held-out manuscripts belong to the task-setter and the judge alone: the sparring-partner, the tuner and the diagnostician do not read any of them.

Put back. The sparring-partner puts the kept worker back by continuing rw_313df9cf84a4 from its newest checkpoint with it and running that round; the judge approves the release only after it. The tuner writes the kept worker's two worker.json files with `worker show` (passing `worker check`) into its release with what it changed. There is no pull request to HuTian-Workers in this round; that comes after the last round.

Every world you run: the full configuration of the world it continues with only the worker of paper-repo and internal-review-repo changed, and "resources": [] written out; budget.total_seconds 1800, at most 12 turns and 1800 model seconds. Note from the last world: a verifier batch once hung in the judge's sandbox (pymupdf loads onnxruntime, whose thread affinity fails under the sandbox's CPU set); the world ends such a turn, and a run can be retried. This world ends at its wall-clock budget; have the release done well before it.

issue.author: ht-admin
issue.body:
Second round on the paper-writing worker of the positions paper-repo and internal-review-repo of the research world rw_313df9cf84a4 (PaperWrite-Bench paper_29, given to you to read), starting from what the first round delivered: the diagnosis, the rubric and the held-out protocol, and the candidates cand-a and cand-b (a CLAUDE.md asset with writing and review norms; cand-b also at higher effort), whose paper_29 runs scored 0.79-0.82, within the incumbent's range. The incumbent is still a-green-hand-jack/HuTian-Workers:incumbent@v3 (Claude Code, claude-sonnet-5-5, effort low). The goal is a worker that really writes better papers; keeping the incumbent is a result only if no candidate wins before this world's wall clock ends.

The held-out world changed: rw_557d19f77f34 could not be continued from c0 (a world problem, recorded and fixed apart from this world). Its replacement is rw_19be25bd2f7d, the same paper_39 (ACL 2025) task, given to you to read, checkpoint c0, never run; continuing it from c0 was checked. The held-out paper's writing material, exactly what the benchmark gives its writers, is now the resource heldout-material (paper_39/), so the judge can check every manuscript's numbers and claims against the source. rw_19be25bd2f7d, the heldout-material resource, the verifier files of paper_39 and every world made from rw_19be25bd2f7d belong to the task-setter and the judge alone: the judge runs the held-out worlds itself, and the sparring-partner, the tuner and the diagnostician do not read any of them.

Comparison and decision: run the incumbent and each candidate at least five times each on the held-out paper, all from c0 of rw_19be25bd2f7d and all at the same time, judged as the protocol says (verifier reward with every component, and the blind rubric). Keep a candidate only if both hold on the held-out paper: its blind writing-quality score is above the incumbent's by more than the spread of the runs, and its verifier reward is not below the incumbent's. If no candidate passes, make a new round of at most two candidates from what the judging shows, and compare again, until one passes or this world's wall clock runs out; at least one candidate in every round changes writing content through assets, and one that changes only effort says so.

Put back and publish, as before: put the kept worker back by continuing rw_313df9cf84a4 from its newest checkpoint with it and running that round; the judge approves the release only after it. Publish the kept worker to a-green-hand-jack/HuTian-Workers by a pull request through the github resource: its worker.json written by `worker show` and passing `worker check`, beside a README.md that says what it changed against incumbent@v3 and by how much on which measures (writing quality and each verifier component, with the spread); if the incumbent is kept, the README says why and on which measures the difference stayed within the spread.

Every world you run: the full configuration of the world it continues with only the worker of paper-repo and internal-review-repo changed, and "resources": [] written out (a world made here without it gets this world's resources, the held-out material among them); budget.total_seconds 1800, at most 12 turns and 1800 model seconds. This world ends at its wall-clock budget; have the release and the pull request done well before it.

issue.author: ht-admin
issue.body:
Improve the paper-writing worker of the positions paper-repo and internal-review-repo of the research world rw_313df9cf84a4, given to you to read. It is a writing-only world made from PaperWrite-Bench task paper_29 (write a 10-page ICLR 2025 paper from the supplied overview, figures, tables and bibliography, into workspace/submission/manuscript.tex and manuscript.pdf; no experiments, no internet). Both incumbents are a-green-hand-jack/HuTian-Workers:incumbent@v3 (Claude Code, claude-sonnet-5-5, effort low). The goal is a worker that really writes better papers, not one that writes this paper better.

What is already measured: the incumbent ran three times on paper_29 from the checkpoint c0 of rw_313df9cf84a4 (c0 is that world before any turn): rw_313df9cf84a4 itself and rw_ec90a7b1da48, rw_017cc0de3d32 (the same state root). Each took about 3.5 minutes, one writing turn and one review that approved at once; a single Claude Code with the same model and effort, without positions, took the same time. The benchmark's verifier gave 0.794, 0.820 and 0.805 (26, 42 and 33 of the 149 references cited). The verifier and the files to run it are in your inputs (verifier/README.md); it measures form and citation coverage, not writing quality.

Training and held-out: paper_29 is for training: diagnosis and candidates are made from it. The held-out paper is PaperWrite-Bench paper_39 (ACL 2025), the world rw_557d19f77f34 given to you to read, checkpoint c0, never run. It belongs to the task-setter and the judge alone: the task-setter keeps its tasks in its repository files and the judge runs them; the tuner and the diagnostician do not read rw_557d19f77f34, its verifier files, or any world made from it.

Judging: the judge scores every manuscript (1) with the verifier, recording the reward and every component, and (2) for writing quality with a rubric the task-setter writes and the judge applies the same way to every manuscript, blind to which worker wrote it (label the manuscripts at random before reading, unblind after scoring). The rubric says that citing references for coverage rather than for what the text says (dumping the bibliography) is recognised and penalised; a gain in citation coverage counts only where the citations fit their context.

Candidates: at most two in a round, each Claude Code with claude-sonnet-5-5, changing the worker's content: files in its assets (writing norms or a skill: structure, use of citations, a self-check list), Claude Code's native settings, or effort. At least one candidate changes writing content through assets, not only effort; a candidate that changes only effort says so in its record.

Comparison and decision: run the incumbent and each candidate three times each on the held-out paper, all from c0 of rw_557d19f77f34 and all at the same time. Keep a candidate only if both hold on the held-out paper: its blind writing-quality score is above the incumbent's by more than the spread of the runs, and its verifier reward is not below the incumbent's. Held-out tasks on paper_29 material may be added as a supplement; the decision rests on paper_39. If no candidate passes and time is left, make another round of candidates.

Put back and publish: put the kept worker back by continuing rw_313df9cf84a4 from its newest checkpoint with it and running that round; the judge approves the release only after it. Publish the kept worker to a-green-hand-jack/HuTian-Workers by a pull request through the github resource: its worker.json written by `worker show` and passing `worker check`, beside a README.md that says what it changed against incumbent@v3 and by how much on which measures (writing quality and each verifier component, with the spread); if the incumbent is kept, the README says why and on which measures the difference stayed within the spread.

Every world you run: the configuration of the world it continues with only the worker of paper-repo and internal-review-repo changed (resources stay empty as there), budget.total_seconds 1800, at most 12 turns and 1800 model seconds. issue.body:
Round 1 of at least three on the paper-writing worker of the positions paper-repo and internal-review-repo of the research world rw_313df9cf84a4 (PaperWrite-Bench paper_29, given to you to read). The aim over the rounds is a curve: each round's kept worker writes better than the last. This world is one round: one diagnosis, at most two candidates, one comparison, one decision.

Where we start. The last world kept cand-a, now published and merged in a-green-hand-jack/HuTian-Workers as cand-a-writer@v1 (paper-repo) and cand-a-reviewer@v1 (internal-review-repo): incumbent@v3 (Claude Code, claude-sonnet-5-5, effort low) plus a CLAUDE.md of writing and review norms. On the held-out paper it raised the blind score from 26.4 to 30.8 of 32 and the verifier reward from 0.886 to 0.900, but it writes longer papers (11 pages in 2 of 5 runs against the 9-page target) and its section_score fell from 0.96 to 0.88. cand-a is the incumbent of this round; the original incumbent@v3 is the curve's origin.

The rubric first. The 32-point rubric can no longer decide: cand-a's mean 30.8 plus its spread 2.0 is above the maximum, so no candidate could ever pass. Before anyone looks at a manuscript made in this world, the task-setter writes rubric v2 with room above cand-a. Its items and the levels of each item come from what the task and the benchmark ask of a paper: the page limit and venue in each task's metadata and template, the required sections the task instruction lists (abstract, introduction, related work, method, experiments, limitations, conclusion), the template's format kept, every claim grounded in the supplied overview, the supplied figures and tables used and interpreted, citations from the given bibliography that fit their sentences; plus how well the paper argues and reads. Every level has an anchored description so two judges would give the same score. It must apply unchanged to any PaperWrite-Bench paper (numbers such as the page limit are read from each task), not only paper_29 or paper_39, and it must not be shaped around cand-a's weaknesses. Freeze it: put it in the task-setter's release with its sha256, and do not change it in this or any later round. Scores under the old rubric stay as they are, for the record.

Diagnosis. The sparring-partner runs the incumbent cand-a twice on the training paper, continuing rw_313df9cf84a4 from c0, for the diagnostician; the diagnostician diagnoses what cand-a still does badly in writing, from those runs, from the earlier paper_29 runs, and from the judge's summary of the last world's comparison (aggregate scores per worker and item, no held-out manuscripts). The tuner makes at most two candidates from the diagnosis, each starting from cand-a: only the worker's content and settings change (assets, instructions, effort and other settings of Claude Code); the agent and the model stay Claude Code and claude-sonnet-5-5; at least one candidate changes writing content through assets, and one that changes only a setting says so. Nothing in a candidate may be about a particular paper.

Comparison and decision. The judge runs, from c0 of rw_19be25bd2f7d (paper_39, ACL 2025) and all at the same time, five runs each of incumbent@v3, cand-a and every candidate: twenty worlds with two candidates. If the provider answers with overloads or the host refuses, start them in two batches with the same mix of workers and say so. Judge every manuscript with the frozen rubric v2, blind (random labels before reading, unblinded after all are scored), and with the verifier (reward and every component), as before. Keep a candidate only if its blind mean under v2 is above cand-a's mean by more than cand-a's spread (max minus min of its runs) and its verifier mean is not below cand-a's; if both pass, keep the better and say why; if none passes, cand-a stays and the record says on which measures the difference stayed within the spread. Record for every worker the v2 blind mean, min, max and spread, the mean of each item, and the verifier mean, min, max and every component, in a round summary in the judge's repository. After the decision is recorded, the diagnostician and the tuner may read that summary for the next round, but not the manuscripts.

Who reads what. rw_19be25bd2f7d, every world made from it, the heldout-material resource, the paper_39 verifier files in your inputs and the held-out manuscripts belong to the task-setter and the judge alone: the sparring-partner, the tuner and the diagnostician do not read any of them.

What happens: 'researchworld continue rw_557d19f77f34 --checkpoint c0 --config <world's effective config, budget 1800/12/1800, roles replaced>' fails every time (9 tries, with and without --exporter current, loaded and unloaded host): "rw_557d19f77f34's own exporter failed: the throwaway Forgejo stopped before it answered". The same command on rw_313df9cf84a4 works. 'status' and 'checkpoints' of rw_557d19f77f34 read fine (checkpoints: before-stop-4ed882f1, c0). Do you know of anything particular about this world (how it was made/stopped), or a way to export it? Waiting on this: the held-out runs; the judge's decision depends on them. Note for whoever drives these worlds: one 'execute --loop' ends 'idle' before the review; run it a second time to reach world-complete (details in runs/README.md of sparring-partner).
issue.title: Continuing the held-out world rw_557d19f77f34 from c0 fails: its throwaway Forgejo stops

comments.author: task-setter
comments.body: I know nothing special about how rw_557d19f77f34 was made or stopped, and I reproduced your failure from my side. Observed: (1) 'continue --checkpoint c0 --config <effective, total_seconds 1800> [--without-frozen-jobs]' -> 'the throwaway Forgejo stopped before it answered'. (2) 'continue --checkpoint before-stop-4ed882f1 --exporter current' -> 'export failed: HTTP 404'. (3) 'researchworld export rw_557d19f77f34 --checkpoint c0 --output DIR' -> the same Forgejo-stopped error, while the same export on rw_313df9cf84a4 c0 works (2 repos, 53 files). So the fault is in this world's c0 snapshot/state, not in your command or the config; I have no docker or state-root access to look inside, and nothing I own can rebuild it. I am not offering a substitute paper_39 world: I have no inputs to make one. This needs the coach to report it as a world problem and ask the host owner (ht-admin) for a repaired or re-made paper_39 c0. I am leaving this open because it is not answered; I am raising it with coach.

issue.author: ht-admin
issue.body:
Improve the paper-writing worker of the positions paper-repo and internal-review-repo of the research world rw_313df9cf84a4, given to you to read. It is a writing-only world made from PaperWrite-Bench task paper_29 (write a 10-page ICLR 2025 paper from the supplied overview, figures, tables and bibliography, into workspace/submission/manuscript.tex and manuscript.pdf; no experiments, no internet). Both incumbents are a-green-hand-jack/HuTian-Workers:incumbent@v3 (Claude Code, claude-sonnet-5-5, effort low). The goal is a worker that really writes better papers, not one that writes this paper better.

What is already measured: the incumbent ran three times on paper_29 from the checkpoint c0 of rw_313df9cf84a4 (c0 is that world before any turn): rw_313df9cf84a4 itself and rw_ec90a7b1da48, rw_017cc0de3d32 (the same state root). Each took about 3.5 minutes, one writing turn and one review that approved at once; a single Claude Code with the same model and effort, without positions, took the same time. The benchmark's verifier gave 0.794, 0.820 and 0.805 (26, 42 and 33 of the 149 references cited). The verifier and the files to run it are in your inputs (verifier/README.md); it measures form and citation coverage, not writing quality.

Training and held-out: paper_29 is for training: diagnosis and candidates are made from it. The held-out paper is PaperWrite-Bench paper_39 (ACL 2025), the world rw_557d19f77f34 given to you to read, checkpoint c0, never run. It belongs to the task-setter and the judge alone: the task-setter keeps its tasks in its repository files and the judge runs them; the tuner and the diagnostician do not read rw_557d19f77f34, its verifier files, or any world made from it.

Judging: the judge scores every manuscript (1) with the verifier, recording the reward and every component, and (2) for writing quality with a rubric the task-setter writes and the judge applies the same way to every manuscript, blind to which worker wrote it (label the manuscripts at random before reading, unblind after scoring). The rubric says that citing references for coverage rather than for what the text says (dumping the bibliography) is recognised and penalised; a gain in citation coverage counts only where the citations fit their context.

Candidates: at most two in a round, each Claude Code with claude-sonnet-5-5, changing the worker's content: files in its assets (writing norms or a skill: structure, use of citations, a self-check list), Claude Code's native settings, or effort. At least one candidate changes writing content through assets, not only effort; a candidate that changes only effort says so in its record.

Comparison and decision: run the incumbent and each candidate three times each on the held-out paper, all from c0 of rw_557d19f77f34 and all at the same time. Keep a candidate only if both hold on the held-out paper: its blind writing-quality score is above the incumbent's by more than the spread of the runs, and its verifier reward is not below the incumbent's. Held-out tasks on paper_29 material may be added as a supplement; the decision rests on paper_39. If no candidate passes and time is left, make another round of candidates.

Put back and publish: put the kept worker back by continuing rw_313df9cf84a4 from its newest checkpoint with it and running that round; the judge approves the release only after it. Publish the kept worker to a-green-hand-jack/HuTian-Workers by a pull request through the github resource: its worker.json written by `worker show` and passing `worker check`, beside a README.md that says what it changed against incumbent@v3 and by how much on which measures (writing quality and each verifier component, with the spread); if the incumbent is kept, the README says why and on which measures the difference stayed within the spread.

Every world you run: the configuration of the world it continues with only the worker of paper-repo and internal-review-repo changed (resources stay empty as there), budget.total_seconds 1800, at most 12 turns and 1800 model seconds. This world itself ends at its wall-clock budget; plan to have the release and the pull request done well before it.

issue.author: ht-admin
issue.body:
Round 1 of at least three on the paper-writing worker of the positions paper-repo and internal-review-repo of the research world rw_313df9cf84a4 (PaperWrite-Bench paper_29, given to you to read). The aim over the rounds is a curve: each round's kept worker writes better than the last. This world is one round: one diagnosis, at most two candidates, one comparison, one decision.

Where we start. The last world kept cand-a, now published and merged in a-green-hand-jack/HuTian-Workers as cand-a-writer@v1 (paper-repo) and cand-a-reviewer@v1 (internal-review-repo): incumbent@v3 (Claude Code, claude-sonnet-5-5, effort low) plus a CLAUDE.md of writing and review norms. On the held-out paper it raised the blind score from 26.4 to 30.8 of 32 and the verifier reward from 0.886 to 0.900, but it writes longer papers (11 pages in 2 of 5 runs against the 9-page target) and its section_score fell from 0.96 to 0.88. cand-a is the incumbent of this round; the original incumbent@v3 is the curve's origin.

The rubric first. The 32-point rubric can no longer decide: cand-a's mean 30.8 plus its spread 2.0 is above the maximum, so no candidate could ever pass. Before anyone looks at a manuscript made in this world, the task-setter writes rubric v2 with room above cand-a. Its items and the levels of each item come from what the task and the benchmark ask of a paper: the page limit and venue in each task's metadata and template, the required sections the task instruction lists (abstract, introduction, related work, method, experiments, limitations, conclusion), the template's format kept, every claim grounded in the supplied overview, the supplied figures and tables used and interpreted, citations from the given bibliography that fit their sentences; plus how well the paper argues and reads. Every level has an anchored description so two judges would give the same score. It must apply unchanged to any PaperWrite-Bench paper (numbers such as the page limit are read from each task), not only paper_29 or paper_39, and it must not be shaped around cand-a's weaknesses. Freeze it: put it in the task-setter's release with its sha256, and do not change it in this or any later round. Scores under the old rubric stay as they are, for the record.

Diagnosis. The sparring-partner runs the incumbent cand-a twice on the training paper, continuing rw_313df9cf84a4 from c0, for the diagnostician; the diagnostician diagnoses what cand-a still does badly in writing, from those runs, from the earlier paper_29 runs, and from the judge's summary of the last world's comparison (aggregate scores per worker and item, no held-out manuscripts). The tuner makes at most two candidates from the diagnosis, each starting from cand-a: only the worker's content and settings change (assets, instructions, effort and other settings of Claude Code); the agent and the model stay Claude Code and claude-sonnet-5-5; at least one candidate changes writing content through assets, and one that changes only a setting says so. Nothing in a candidate may be about a particular paper.

Comparison and decision. The judge runs, from c0 of rw_19be25bd2f7d (paper_39, ACL 2025) and all at the same time, five runs each of incumbent@v3, cand-a and every candidate: twenty worlds with two candidates. If the provider answers with overloads or the host refuses, start them in two batches with the same mix of workers and say so. Judge every manuscript with the frozen rubric v2, blind (random labels before reading, unblinded after all are scored), and with the verifier (reward and every component), as before. Keep a candidate only if its blind mean under v2 is above cand-a's mean by more than cand-a's spread (max minus min of its runs) and its verifier mean is not below cand-a's; if both pass, keep the better and say why; if none passes, cand-a stays and the record says on which measures the difference stayed within the spread. Record for every worker the v2 blind mean, min, max and spread, the mean of each item, and the verifier mean, min, max and every component, in a round summary in the judge's repository. After the decision is recorded, the diagnostician and the tuner may read that summary for the next round, but not the manuscripts.

Who reads what. rw_19be25bd2f7d, every world made from it, the heldout-material resource, the paper_39 verifier files in your inputs and the held-out manuscripts belong to the task-setter and the judge alone: the sparring-partner, the tuner and the diagnostician do not read any of them.

Put back. The sparring-partner puts the kept worker back by continuing rw_313df9cf84a4 from its newest checkpoint with it and running that round; the judge approves the release only after it. The tuner writes the kept worker's two worker.json files with `worker show` (passing `worker check`) into its release with what it changed. There is no pull request to HuTian-Workers in this round; that comes after the last round.

Every world you run: the full configuration of the world it continues with only the worker of paper-repo and internal-review-repo changed, and "resources": [] written out; budget.total_seconds 1800, at most 12 turns and 1800 model seconds. Note from the last world: a verifier batch once hung in the judge's sandbox (pymupdf loads onnxruntime, whose thread affinity fails under the sandbox's CPU set); the world ends such a turn, and a run can be retried. This world ends at its wall-clock budget; have the release done well before it.
